# discord_channel_permission_overwrite (Resource)

Manages a single permission overwrite on a Discord channel for a role or member. Read through the parent channel, since Discord exposes no standalone overwrite endpoint.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "discord_channel_permission_overwrite" "mods_can_manage" {
  channel_id   = "123456789012345678"
  overwrite_id = "987654321098765432" # a role or member ID
  type         = "role"

  allow = ["VIEW_CHANNEL", "MANAGE_MESSAGES"]
  deny  = ["SEND_MESSAGES"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `channel_id` (String) Snowflake ID of the channel. Changing this forces a new overwrite.
- `overwrite_id` (String) Snowflake ID of the role or member the overwrite applies to. Changing this forces a new overwrite.
- `type` (String) Overwrite target type: `role` or `member`. Changing this forces a new overwrite.

### Optional

- `allow` (Set of String) Set of Discord permission names explicitly allowed by this overwrite.
- `deny` (Set of String) Set of Discord permission names explicitly denied by this overwrite.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Synthetic ID in the form `channel_id:overwrite_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Permission overwrites are imported using "channel_id:overwrite_id".
terraform import discord_channel_permission_overwrite.mods_can_manage 123456789012345678:987654321098765432
```
